You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 8ddec8b82f90652182cb7eddb7aa841e4fa4e639 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Morris Jette <jette@schedmd.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jul 2013 16:29:10 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] Fix for batch job CPU count if --ntasks-per-node specified

and max_nodes == min_nodes or no max_nodes specified
bug introduced in commit 1b7f5b91c18e747dd4a27fc1f64c000f04e78669
fix for bug 343
---
 src/sbatch/opt.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/src/sbatch/opt.c b/src/sbatch/opt.c
index 7101b7b412..57cb0803c4 100644
--- a/src/sbatch/opt.c
+++ b/src/sbatch/opt.c
@@ -2145,7 +2145,7 @@ static bool _opt_verify(void)
 				      opt.overcommit, 0);
 
 	if ((opt.ntasks_per_node > 0) && (!opt.ntasks_set) &&
-	    (opt.max_nodes == 0)) {
+	    ((opt.max_nodes == 0) || (opt.min_nodes == opt.max_nodes))) {
 		opt.ntasks = opt.min_nodes * opt.ntasks_per_node;
 		opt.ntasks_set = 1;
 	}
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by an incorrect condition in the code that determined the number of tasks for batch jobs when the `--ntasks-per-node` option was specified. Specifically, the original condition only checked if `max_nodes` was zero, which did not account for the scenario where `max_nodes` and `min_nodes` were equal. This oversight led to incorrect calculations of the total number of tasks when both `max_nodes` and `min_nodes` were set to the same value, resulting in potential misconfiguration of job resources. The patch corrects this by adding a check to ensure that the condition also accounts for the case where `min_nodes` equals `max_nodes`.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect condition in the code that determined the number of tasks for batch jobs when the `--ntasks-per-node` option was specified. Specifically, the original condition only checked if `max_nodes` was zero, which did not account for the scenario where `max_nodes` and `min_nodes` were equal. This oversight led to incorrect calculations of the total number of tasks when both `max_nodes` and `min_nodes` were set to the same value, resulting in potential misconfiguration of job resources. The patch corrects this by adding a check to ensure that the condition also accounts for the case where `min_nodes` equals `max_nodes`.
